opening_message:
Ticket 1: Haley Roberts (employee ID E021) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E021.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Haley Roberts (E021) is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so write access is within policy. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Haley Roberts (E021) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Basic training caps access at read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: The Security note states Haley Roberts (E021) is a contractor with basic security training (Security DB), which caps contractor access at read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed for contractors). The requested write exceeds that maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted. Note: the HR note claims full-time Engineer, but the Security record explicitly contradicts this and indicates contractor status, so the more restrictive contractor policy applies.
